clue.text: Air and fuel are mixed in this vehicle by an Italian pistol maker, reportedly

definitions.text: Air and fuel are mixed in this
definitions.note: a description of the device rather than a noun

indicators.note: one thing set by another sits beside it, so the two pieces stand side by side
what is reported is what people say, so we go by the spoken sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: an everyday vehicle
Beretta is the famous Italian firearms company

explanation.surface: A gun-maker's car with an engine where air and fuel get mixed.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'car Beretta' quickly and you hear the engine part; the spelling of the second half changes completely to fit CARBURETTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: In a petrol engine this component blends incoming air with fuel vapour before combustion in the cylinders.

clue.text: CO2 emissions from wagon carrying fluid pint of boron

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it inside, so one piece goes within another
a fluid thing has no fixed shape, so these letters can flow into a new order

blocks.note: a cart is a simple wagon
taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pollution coming from a cart that carries a pint of an element, mixing chemistry with transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'CO2 emissions' looks like part of the chemistry scene with boron, but it is the definition; the wagon is split to hold the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase measures the total greenhouse gas a person, product or activity releases, chiefly counted as carbon dioxide.

clue.text: Yammer on endlessly to teacher

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at length

explanation.surface: Someone droning on and on to their teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English to 'rabbit on' means to chatter tediously, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk; drop its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbi literally means 'my master' and is the title of a Jewish religious scholar who instructs a congregation.

clue.text: Skyward tendency of prudent bats

indicators.note: someone bats is crazy, so these letters have gone mad and lost their order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Careful bats tend to fly upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' reads as flying animals, but it is the slang adjective for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising movement over time, in prices or figures, is called this; skyward means upward and tendency means trend.

clue.text: We hear you're on the largest continent — it's even bigger than that!

definitions.note: a description rather than a noun

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound, so the spelling may differ
in a down entry one thing on another sits above it, so the pieces follow in order

blocks.note: the contraction of you are
the biggest of the continents

explanation.surface: Telling someone they are on the biggest continent, then correcting that it is bigger still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You're Asia' said aloud is the name of the larger landmass; 'that' points back to Asia, which this combined area exceeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe and Asia together form one continuous landmass, which naturally outsizes Asia alone.

clue.text: Send pictures back with assorted mints

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters are read in reverse
one thing with another is alongside it, so the pieces are joined
assorted things are mixed together, so these letters come in a jumbled order

blocks.note: pictures collectively are art
taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Returning some photos along with a box of mixed sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send' looks like the start of an instruction, but it is the definition, and 'back' turns ART round rather than sending anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a message or signal from one place to another is to dispatch it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Verbally control pets and come down heavily

indicators.note: done verbally means spoken, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: to rein is to control, and cats and dogs are typical pets

explanation.surface: Keeping your animals in line by voice, then collapsing heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: Rein and the weather word sound alike, so 'rein in the cats and dogs' becomes the idiom for a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a torrential downpour, when the weather pours water from the sky in great quantity.

clue.text: Inhumane routine is observed in revolutionary scientist's workplace

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters run backwards
to be seen in a place is to be inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a laboratory, where scientists work
a rut is a dull fixed routine

explanation.surface: Cruel daily procedures carried out in a radical scientist's laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' sounds like a description of the scientist, but it only turns the workplace round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe savage, cruel treatment lacking any compassion or pity.

clue.text: Mixed choir has energy that's impressive

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it alongside, so the pieces join up
mixed things are stirred together, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A choir of men and women sings with energy, which is impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed choir' suggests male and female voices; here it means the letters of choir, plus E, are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave, grand feat that commands admiration can be called this; the sense of awe-inspiring is shared.

clue.text: Cheese on toast? Bloody small piece!

blocks.note: rare steak is bloody, barely cooked
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated at being served a tiny portion of cheese on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' reads as a British swear word of annoyance, but it describes undercooked meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted seasoned cheese served over toasted bread, a classic British snack.

clue.text: Appreciate lies are wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place and need putting right

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moral lesson: understand that lying is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a complete moral statement, so 'are' hides as fodder rather than grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate a fact is to become fully aware of it or understand it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: They cheat on their partners twice without the first sign of regret

indicators.note: a first sign is an opening mark, so only the initial letter is kept
in its old sense without means outside, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: twice means two times
the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: Serial cheats betray their partners again and again without a shred of remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means 'outside', the old sense, so the phrase for twice goes round the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are unfaithful by secretly seeing someone else besides their lover are called this colloquially.

clue.text: Rampant oiks surround Conservative pervert

indicators.note: something rampant runs wild and out of control, so these letters scatter
to surround is to encircle, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: oiks are uncouth louts in British slang; taken here as letters
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A gang of rowdy yobs mob a Tory politician who is a pervert.
explanation.walkthrough: An oik is British slang for a crude, uncouth person; the word is used only for its letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a sick-minded or depraved person, someone with disturbed or deviant tastes.

clue.text: Elevator strongly illuminated outside

indicators.note: being outside something means wrapping round it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: lit means lighted up
f is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong

explanation.surface: A lift brightly lit up on the outside of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: F stands for forte, the musical marking for loudly or strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevator is the American word; British English calls the cabin carrying people between floors by this name.

clue.text: Visionary's italicised translation

indicators.note: a translation renders words in a new form, so these letters are recast

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A visionary writer's work, translated and printed in italics.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive, but it is short for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe someone guided by lofty ideals and dreams of how things could be, rather than practicalities.

clue.text: And not subsequently welcoming resistance, like Alan Bennett or Victoria Wood, for example

definitions.text: like Alan Bennett or Victoria Wood, for example

indicators.note: welcoming a guest means taking them in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: nor means and not
then means afterwards
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A comment on the regional character of two much-loved English writers and comedians.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Bennett is a playwright from Leeds and Victoria Wood a comedian from Lancashire, both famous for their northern English voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Both come from the north of England, and their humour is rooted in that region's speech and life.

clue.text: Rebel cool cats in disarray

indicators.note: things in a state of disarray are untidy and jumbled, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, doing double duty in the surface

explanation.surface: A rebellious crowd of hip, trendy people in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In disarray' reads as one phrase, but the 'in' is part of the fodder and only 'disarray' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions is a nonconformist who defies convention.

clue.text: Infantry leader takes up arms and flags

indicators.note: the leader goes in front, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: the opening letter
rebels who take up arms rise up

explanation.surface: An army officer leads the infantry into battle, raising weapons and banners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like banners in a military scene, but yellow and blue flags are names for wild iris plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a traditional name for several iris species, especially the yellow water iris growing by ponds.

clue.text: Boisterous girl let date run wild

indicators.note: things that run wild go out of control, so the letters break formation

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rowdy young woman lets her romantic evening get out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladette is British slang from the 1990s for a young woman who drinks and behaves as rowdily as the lads.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a young woman behaving in a loud, laddish, hard-drinking way, so rowdy fits.

clue.text: Sucking sound obscured HQ's clue

indicators.note: something obscured is muddled so it cannot be read plainly, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy hears a muffled noise that hides headquarters' secret hint.
explanation.walkthrough: The rare Q in 'HQ's' is a strong hint that the letters must be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the wet noise made when boots pull out of mud, a soft suction noise.

clue.text: Pull over to identify urban district

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A police officer stops a car to check which part of town it belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull over' reads as the motoring phrase, but 'over' is split off to turn the verb round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward is an electoral or administrative division of a city or borough.

clue.text: Second in command put dye all over the place

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An assistant has spilled dye everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second in command' could be read as an order given, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is the person ranking just below a leader who stands in for them when absent.

clue.text: Putin's ridiculous contribution

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurdly out of shape, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: the Russian president's name, taken as letters

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Russian leader has made an absurd contribution.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is not possessive; it stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone puts into a shared effort, such as ideas, advice or work offered.

clue.text: Increased by 100% and in real agony

blocks.note: first meaning: made twice as large
second meaning: bent over with pain

explanation.surface: Pain that has suddenly become twice as bad.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests one worsening condition; the phrase separately means multiplied by two and folded over in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both making something twice as large and bending forward in severe pain or laughter.

clue.text: Girl gets old rope

indicators.note: to get something is to acquire it and add it on, so the pieces join

blocks.note: a lass is a girl
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A girl is given a worn piece of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Lass is a northern British and Scottish word for a girl or young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped cowboy's rope with a running noose for catching cattle.

clue.text: Famous US rapper nearly joins the National Trust

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
joining means attaching end to end, so the pieces are placed together

blocks.note: Eminem is the well-known Detroit rapper
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust

explanation.surface: A celebrated American rapper almost becomes a member of a British heritage charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes someone distinguished and well known, respected for achievement in a field.

clue.text: Burnt remains concealed by thug's attack

indicators.note: something concealed by another is covered and wrapped by it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a lout is a thug
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Evidence of a fire hidden by a hooligan who attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concealed by' suggests a hidden word, but the ash is placed inside a word for a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to strike suddenly or verbally assail someone, a phrasal verb for violent assault.

clue.text: Marquee attracts cavorting hookers — on which you wait nervously

indicators.note: to attract something is to draw it alongside, so the pieces join
cavorting means leaping about wildly, so these letters jump out of order

blocks.note: a marquee is a large tent
taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A party tent draws a lively crowd of sex workers, which makes someone anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'on tenterhooks' means anxiously waiting; tenterhooks were hooks for stretching cloth on a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on tenterhooks is the idiom for anxious suspense, so these are what one waits on figuratively.
